input.rationale: Fix one attributed responsibility on the configuration path and run a first direct check for it. Reading Raft.appendConfigurationEntry shows that the leader publishes a new configuration through setLatestConfiguration(configuration, future.Index()), recomputes the commitment voter set and restarts replication after dispatchLogs, without inspecting the dispatch outcome; dispatchLogs assigns the index and pushes the future before StoreLogs and, on a StoreLogs error, answers the future and steps down to Follower. The obligation is therefore that a server must not treat a configuration as its latest unless the entry was durably stored, and the check drives exactly that path with one injected durable-write failure.

candidate.rationale: The configuration-append path publishes configuration state without checking whether the supporting log entry was durably stored, so the voter set used for quorum and eligibility can diverge from the agreed log. This is a sourced responsibility on the A4 configuration path with a stated A1 consequence, and it is executable with an injectable LogStore.

question.question: When a leader attempts a configuration change and the configuration entry's durable log write fails, must the server keep its latest configuration equal to the configuration that is actually present in its log, rather than adopting the new voter set?
question.importance: The latest configuration defines the voter set used for election eligibility, the commitment quorum and the leader-lease check, so a server that adopts an unpersisted configuration can compute quorums over a membership that was never agreed in the log; on a node that later regains leadership this can commit a configuration that no log entry supports.
contexts: stable single-voter leader whose next durable log write fails
configuration change admitted once latest==committed and the leader has committed an entry of its term
event_paths: Raft.appendConfigurationEntry -> Raft.dispatchLogs fails StoreLogs, answers the future and sets state Follower, then returns to appendConfigurationEntry

supporting_behavior_ids.b-commit-quorum: consumes the latest voter set as the commitment quorum, the A1 consequence of adopting an unpersisted configuration

counterevidence: configurationChangeChIfStable admits only one uncommitted configuration at a time, which keeps ordinary membership changes well ordered
a subsequent successful AppendEntries from a working leader replaces the log and the latest configuration, so an isolated duplication usually self-heals
unknowns: Whether the phantom latest configuration can actually be committed by this node if it regains leadership before the log is repaired
question.trigger_rationale: appendConfigurationEntry publishes the new configuration through setLatestConfiguration and commitment.setConfiguration immediately after dispatchLogs, while dispatchLogs can fail the durable write and step the node down; the publish happens regardless of that outcome, so the attempt event and the post-failure configuration observation are the decisive pair.

obligation.description: A server must not publish or commit a configuration change as its latest configuration unless the corresponding configuration log entry was durably stored, so that the voter set used for quorum, election eligibility and the leader lease always corresponds to an entry present in the log or snapshot.

scope.description: One configuration change attempted by a stable leader whose durable log write for that configuration entry fails.
assumptions: configurationChangeChIfStable has admitted the request (latest==committed and the leader has committed an entry of its term)
the only faulted component is the LogStore's StoreLogs call
excluded: consequences that require the node to regain leadership and commit the phantom configuration
failures of StableStore, the transport or the snapshot store

pending: The whole-cluster consequence of a phantom latest configuration is retained as an open question, not established by this unit.

grounding.derivation: configurations.latest is documented as the latest configuration in the log or snapshot and latestIndex as the index where it was written; processConfigurationLogEntry is the intended writer from an actual entry, and setLatestConfiguration is meant to mirror the configuration that a log entry established. appendConfigurationEntry reaches setLatestConfiguration unconditionally after dispatchLogs, while dispatchLogs can answer the future with a durable-write error and step the node down, so the responsibility is that the publish must be qualified by that durable write.
grounding.applicability: Applies to a leader attempting a single configuration change when the entry's durable log write fails; the ordinary path with a successful write is unaffected, and the unit does not claim a cluster-wide outcome.
unresolved: Whether the divergence can be turned into a committed configuration by a later leadership change
alternatives: returning before setLatestConfiguration when dispatchLogs reports an error is one design alternative; the obligation fixes the responsibility, not that repair

associations.rationale: This declaration builds the next configuration, dispatches it as a log entry, and then unconditionally publishes it as the latest configuration and recomputes the commitment voter set.

bindings.description: Raft.appendConfigurationEntry: the leader-side membership change path that publishes latest configuration state after dispatchLogs.

result.summary:
Submitted a check product that fixes one attributed responsibility on the configuration path and runs a first direct check for it.

Files (draft-relative): submission.json (submitted product), plan_config_durability.json (DirectCheckPlan), harness_config_durability.go (Go test harness run as assurance_generated_test.go in package "."), plus the already-accepted map.json.

Context from the index: submission 1 was accepted, so map v1 is the accepted basis (A1/A2 core overview usable, 16 behaviors, 6 facts, 4 surfaces) and candidate 2324b095… is now paused by this product.

The new obligation: a server must not publish or commit a configuration change as its latest configuration unless the corresponding configuration log entry was durably stored, so the voter set used for quorum, election eligibility and the leader lease always corresponds to an entry in the log/snapshot. It is grounded in appendConfigurationEntry (raft.go 1203-1240, bound symbol appendConfigurationEntry) which calls dispatchLogs and then unconditionally runs setLatestConfiguration(configuration, future.Index()), commitment.setConfiguration and startStopReplication; dispatchLogs assigns the index and pushes the future before StoreLogs and, on a StoreLogs error, answers the future and sets state Follower.

The discriminator: a stable single-voter leader whose next durable log write (the configuration entry) is failed by an injected LogStore wrapper. The harness admits a config_append_attempt (identity attempt=config-append-1) and, after the failure, reports config_state_after_failure with store_failed, append_error, latest_voter_count, latest_index, committed_index and log_last_index. The implication property says that when store_failed is true the node's latest voter count must still equal the pre-attempt voter count; a violation is a node adopting a voter set whose entry is not in its log. Source citations are limited to raft.go 1203-1240/1244-1291, configuration.go 174-195/228-310 and commitment.go 1-104.

Preflight `validate` returned valid=true with no diagnostics. Acceptance, clean-copy execution, the observed result and any resulting Evidence remain with the controller; local compilation was not possible because only the draft directory is writable, so the harness bytes are fixed but unexecuted in this turn.

question.question: Is a heartbeat delivered through the transport fast path serialized with the main loop before it updates the receiver's term, state and believed leader, or can Raft.appendEntries run concurrently with runFollower/runCandidate on the same instance?
question.importance: The single-writer premise for the authority context (state, currentTerm, leaderAddr/leaderID) is what the whole election and step-down reasoning rests on. If an off-thread heartbeat can mutate that context while the main loop is in the middle of a campaign or a term change, a race could leave a node believing in a different leader/term than its own state machine; the consequence is a wrong authority view rather than a memory-safety crash, so the impact is bounded but the premise matters.

counterevidence: setState and setCurrentTerm use atomic stores and setLeader uses a mutex, so a pure heartbeat does not obviously produce a torn read of any single field
a pure heartbeat carries no entries, no previous-entry index and a zero leader commit index, so it skips the log, configuration and commit branches of appendEntries
unknowns: Which fields a pure heartbeat actually mutates on the receiver, and whether the existing atomic/locked access already provides the needed ordering
Whether the main loop can observe the update while it is inside runCandidate's vote tally rather than only at a select boundary
question.trigger_rationale: Raft.appendEntries is documented as callable only from the main thread, yet NewRaft installs Raft.processHeartbeat (which calls appendEntries) as the transport heartbeat handler, and NetworkTransport.handleConn, started as a goroutine per connection, invokes that handler directly for pure heartbeats. That is a concrete, sourced difference in the authority-context path; bounding which fields a pure heartbeat actually mutates and whether the existing atomic/locked access already serializes them decides whether the comment is stale or the code unsafe.

formation.explanation: The leader appends each accepted command as a local log entry for its term (b-dispatch-logs), then each per-peer replication goroutine pushes AppendEntries and reports the highest index the peer has stored (b-leader-replicate). commitment.match/recalculate turn those per-voter match indexes into a quorum index, refusing to commit anything below the first index appended in the leader's term (b-commit-quorum). When the quorum index advances, the leader loop publishes the new commit index and applies the committed prefix (b-leader-commit-apply). The support is 'qualified' because a match index only counts after the follower's log has been shown to agree with the leader's up to the previous entry.

context.explanation: Authority is scoped to a term and to the voter set of the latest configuration. A follower that stops hearing a leader becomes a candidate (b-heartbeat-timeout); the candidate proposes and persists the next term and asks for votes, optionally after a pre-vote round (b-candidate-election, b-prevote), and becomes leader only on a quorum of current voters. Voters decide with term, membership, an already-persisted vote for the term, and log up-to-date-ness (b-vote-grant). A leader abandons the role when it observes a higher term or cannot contact a quorum of current voters (b-leader-stepdown), and it can hand the role over deliberately with a replicated-then-TimeoutNow transfer (b-leadership-transfer).

connection.explanation: A1 and A2 meet on three sourced points. First, the term-start-index rule in the commitment makes the leader's own new-term entry a precondition for committing anything, so a server that merely won an election cannot commit an earlier leader's entries (b-commit-quorum / f-commit-quorum / f-term-vote). Second, the voter set that defines both a winning quorum and the commitment quorum comes from the latest configuration, so membership changes reshape eligibility and commitment together (b-config-change, b-candidate-election / f-config-membership). Third, a follower only counts as support after its log prefix has been shown to match the leader's, and that same AppendEntries handling carries the term/state transitions; losing the term (b-leader-stepdown) discards the commitment that the old term's support created, while a transfer pushes the target to the leader's last index before handing over. Old work is handled by failing every inflight future with ErrLeadershipLost on step-down, so pending client requests cannot be mistaken for applied decisions.

open_details: The heartbeat fast path (Raft.processHeartbeat, installed by NewRaft and dispatched from NetworkTransport.handleConn) runs appendEntries off the main loop for pure heartbeats; the fields touched are atomic or lock-protected but the ordering against the main loop is unverified.
Raft.timeoutNow campaigns on the target without consulting the request term or sender.
The membership-change error path in appendConfigurationEntry continues to publish the new latest configuration and commitment after a StoreLogs failure that already set state Follower.
after.rationale: Both core lines are read end to end from the leader's append/commit path and from the follower/candidate/voter/step-down path, and their three concrete connections (term-start-index commitment rule, configuration-driven quorum, prefix-validated support with pending-work failure on step-down) are sourced. The remaining items are local anomalies rather than unexplained formation or authority transitions, so the overview is usable while those leads stay open.

after.system_boundary: hashicorp/raft is an embeddable Go library implementing a single Raft consensus group whose replicated state is an application FSM; the library owns leadership/election, log replication, commitment, membership, snapshots and the FSM application loop, while the application owns the FSM, the LogStore/StableStore/SnapshotStore and the Transport (inmem, tcp or network).

question.question: Is a heartbeat delivered through the transport fast path serialized with the main loop before it updates the receiver's term, state and believed leader, or can Raft.appendEntries run concurrently with runFollower/runCandidate on the same instance?
question.importance: The single-writer premise for the authority context (state, currentTerm, leaderAddr/leaderID) is what the whole election and step-down reasoning rests on. If an off-thread heartbeat can mutate that context while the main loop is in the middle of a campaign or a term change, a race could leave a node believing in a different leader/term than its own state machine; the consequence is a wrong authority view rather than a memory-safety crash, so the impact is bounded but the premise matters.

question.trigger_rationale: Raft.appendEntries is documented as callable only from the main thread, yet NewRaft installs Raft.processHeartbeat (which calls appendEntries) as the transport heartbeat handler, and NetworkTransport.handleConn, started as a goroutine per connection, invokes that handler directly for pure heartbeats. That is a concrete, sourced difference in the authority-context path; bounding which fields a pure heartbeat actually mutates and whether the existing atomic/locked access already serializes them decides whether the comment is stale or the code unsafe.

grounding.derivation: configurations.latest is documented as the latest configuration in the log or snapshot and latestIndex as the index where it was written; processConfigurationLogEntry is the intended writer from an actual entry, and setLatestConfiguration is meant to mirror the configuration that a log entry established. appendConfigurationEntry reaches setLatestConfiguration unconditionally after dispatchLogs, while dispatchLogs can answer the future with a durable-write error and step the node down, so the responsibility is that the publish must be qualified by that durable write.

formation.explanation: The leader appends each accepted command as a local log entry for its term (b-dispatch-logs), then each per-peer replication goroutine pushes AppendEntries and reports the highest index the peer has stored (b-leader-replicate). commitment.match/recalculate turn those per-voter match indexes into a quorum index, refusing to commit anything below the first index appended in the leader's term (b-commit-quorum). When the quorum index advances, the leader loop publishes the new commit index and applies the committed prefix (b-leader-commit-apply). The support is 'qualified' because a match index only counts after the follower's log has been shown to agree with the leader's up to the previous entry.

context.explanation: Authority is scoped to a term and to the voter set of the latest configuration. A follower that stops hearing a leader becomes a candidate (b-heartbeat-timeout); the candidate proposes and persists the next term and asks for votes, optionally after a pre-vote round (b-candidate-election, b-prevote), and becomes leader only on a quorum of current voters. Voters decide with term, membership, an already-persisted vote for the term, and log up-to-date-ness (b-vote-grant). A leader abandons the role when it observes a higher term or cannot contact a quorum of current voters (b-leader-stepdown), and it can hand the role over deliberately with a replicated-then-TimeoutNow transfer (b-leadership-transfer).

connection.explanation: A1 and A2 meet on three sourced points. First, the term-start-index rule in the commitment makes the leader's own new-term entry a precondition for committing anything, so a server that merely won an election cannot commit an earlier leader's entries (b-commit-quorum / f-commit-quorum / f-term-vote). Second, the voter set that defines both a winning quorum and the commitment quorum comes from the latest configuration, so membership changes reshape eligibility and commitment together (b-config-change, b-candidate-election / f-config-membership). Third, a follower only counts as support after its log prefix has been shown to match the leader's, and that same AppendEntries handling carries the term/state transitions; losing the term (b-leader-stepdown) discards the commitment that the old term's support created, while a transfer pushes the target to the leader's last index before handing over. Old work is handled by failing every inflight future with ErrLeadershipLost on step-down, so pending client requests cannot be mistaken for applied decisions.

open_details: The heartbeat fast path (Raft.processHeartbeat, installed by NewRaft and dispatched from NetworkTransport.handleConn) runs appendEntries off the main loop for pure heartbeats; the fields touched are atomic or lock-protected but the ordering against the main loop is unverified.
Raft.timeoutNow campaigns on the target without consulting the request term or sender.
The membership-change error path in appendConfigurationEntry continues to publish the new latest configuration and commitment after a StoreLogs failure that already set state Follower.
after.rationale: Both core lines are read end to end from the leader's append/commit path and from the follower/candidate/voter/step-down path, and their three concrete connections (term-start-index commitment rule, configuration-driven quorum, prefix-validated support with pending-work failure on step-down) are sourced. The remaining items are local anomalies rather than unexplained formation or authority transitions, so the overview is usable while those leads stay open.

after.meaning: Committed entries are applied to the FSM exactly once, in index order and without gaps, up to the last applied index.
after.validity_context: Per FSM instance; lastApplied only advances and installed snapshots jump it forward.
after.durability: Depends on the application FSM; the library only guarantees a single ordered application.
after.recovery: An installed or restored snapshot sets lastApplied to the snapshot index before further entries are applied.
unknowns: Whether the FSM itself persists its effect is application-owned and not established here.

after.meaning: A log index in the leader's current term becomes the leader's commitIndex only once a quorum of the voters of the latest configuration is known to hold the log through that index, and never below the first index appended in the leader's current term.

identity.scope: current leader term with the latest configuration's voter set

after.validity_context: Valid while this server is the leader for its current term; the commitment structure is recreated on becoming leader and discarded on step-down.
after.durability: The commit index itself is in-memory; the durable consequence is the applied FSM state.
after.recovery: After restart the commit index is rebuilt from the snapshot and log, and the quorum tracking is rebuilt only when a server becomes leader again.
unknowns: Whether the quorum match index computed over an uncommitted latest configuration can exceed what the committed configuration would allow before that configuration commits.

after.meaning: The latest configuration is taken from the highest-indexed configuration entry in the log or snapshot and determines the voter set used for quorum, election eligibility and lease checks; the committed configuration is the last one known committed.
after.validity_context: Valid for the log/snapshot history this server holds; the latest configuration may be uncommitted.
after.durability: Recovered from the log scan and from a snapshot at startup.
after.recovery: NewRaft scans configuration entries after the snapshot index and installs the snapshot's configuration.

after.meaning: A server acts as leader only while it holds the leadership for the current term; it abandons that role on observing a higher term or on losing contact with a quorum of current voters.

identity.scope: one term with the latest configuration's voter set

after.validity_context: Scoped to a term and the latest configuration's voters; not durable across restarts.
after.durability: Not durable; a restarted server begins again as Follower.
after.recovery: A restarted node relearns the leader from an AppendEntries request or campaign.

after.meaning: When a follower accepts an AppendEntries request it keeps a log that agrees with the leader's on all entries up to the request's previous entry, replacing any conflicting suffix, so a reported match index means real agreement.
after.validity_context: Established per AppendEntries exchange under the current leader term and configuration.
after.durability: Accepted entries are written to the LogStore before success is reported.
after.recovery: After restart the prefix is revalidated by the next AppendEntries, and conflicts are removed with DeleteRange.

after.meaning: The current term is durable and non-decreasing, and a server grants at most one vote per term, only to a candidate whose log is at least as up to date as its own.

identity.object: current term and the vote recorded for it

after.validity_context: Holds across restarts because the term and the vote are persisted in the StableStore before being relied on.
after.durability: Written to StableStore; setCurrentTerm panics on write failure and persistVote returns an error that aborts the caller.
after.recovery: NewRaft reloads CurrentTerm at startup and the last vote is read from StableStore on each RequestVote.

after.reason: Initialization and disaster-recovery entry points have not been traced in this run and are kept as an unread boundary rather than assigned a responsibility.

The transport heartbeat fast path invokes this handler outside the main loop: NewRaft installs it with trans.SetHeartbeatHandler, and NetworkTransport.handleConn (started with 'go') calls the handler directly for pure heartbeats. Raft.appendEntries is documented as main-thread only. Whether the touched fields being atomic or lock-protected makes the off-thread heartbeat safe is not established here.
Handles a TimeoutNowRequest by clearing the leader and campaigning; the request's term and sender are not consulted, which is recorded as an open premise of b-leadership-transfer.
Transport-level plumbing that decides whether a request is fast-pathed to the beacon handler or delivered on the consumer channel; it is not itself a consensus obligation.

after.system_boundary: hashicorp/raft is an embeddable Go library implementing a single Raft consensus group whose replicated state is an application FSM; the library owns leadership/election, log replication, commitment, membership, snapshots and the FSM application loop, while the application owns the FSM, the LogStore/StableStore/SnapshotStore and the Transport (inmem, tcp or network).
protocol_contexts: Leader appends client commands and replicates them to followers (A1).
Followers/candidates/leaders maintain term and leadership context (A2).
Membership configuration (voter/nonvoter) determines quorum and eligibility (A4).
Committed entries are applied to the FSM (A5).
ownership: Per-instance: each Raft object owns its own raftState, configurations, stable store view and leaderState.
Per-term leadership: leaderState (commitment, inflight, replState, notify) is created on becoming leader and destroyed on step-down.
Transport-owned: the network layer decides whether a request is delivered on the main loop or through the optional heartbeat fast path.
selection_injection: The application selects log/stable/snapshot stores, transport, FSM and timeouts via Config.
BatchApplyCh and MaxAppendEntries control group-commit batching.
PreVoteDisabled and transport support select pre-vote behaviour.
variants: BatchingFSM vs single-entry FSM; ConfigurationStore present or not.
inmem vs tcp vs network transport (only the network transport installs the heartbeat fast path).
unknowns: The behaviour of BootstrapCluster/RecoverCluster at initialization and of the raft-compat test module is not yet read in this run.

selections.rationale: Fix one attributed responsibility on the configuration path and run a first direct check for it. Reading Raft.appendConfigurationEntry shows that the leader publishes a new configuration through setLatestConfiguration(configuration, future.Index()), recomputes the commitment voter set and restarts replication after dispatchLogs, without inspecting the dispatch outcome; dispatchLogs assigns the index and pushes the future before StoreLogs and, on a StoreLogs error, answers the future and steps down to Follower. The obligation is therefore that a server must not treat a configuration as its latest unless the entry was durably stored, and the check drives exactly that path with one injected durable-write failure.
